Author: Ravindra Maithani

 High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No. 2670 of 2023
Mahesh Sharma ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Present:-
Mr. Vikas Anand, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. S.C. Dumka, Aga for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant Mahesh Sharma is in judicial custody in Fir No. 592 of 2023, under Sections 376 and 506
Ipc, Police Station Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the applicant introduced himself to the informant with a proposal for marriage.
The applicant, under the pretext of marriage, established physical relations with the informant.
They married on 13.05.2023.
Thereafter, the applicant took the informant to his home and established physical relations with her and also made intimate videos.
Subsequently, the informant came to know that the applicant is already married and is having children.
When questioned, the applicant threatened the victim in the name of making the intimate videos viral.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the case is false; both the applicant and the victim are major; the informant is the wife of the applicant; the applicant did not conceal his first marriage; the informant had the knowledge of first marriage of the applicant; the relationship was consensual.
Reference has been made to the statements of the informant recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code") to argue that there is no concealment of facts.
5. It is the stage of bail.
Much of the discussion is not expected of.
The discussion is being made with a caveat that any observation made in this order should not have any bearing at trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that the statements of the victim are wavering as to how she first came to know that the applicant was already married.
Reference has been made to the version of the FIR and the statements of the informant recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Code.
7. According to the statement under Section 161 of the Code, after the marriage, the informant stayed in the house of the applicant.
After three days, the first wife of the applicant came and threw the articles of the informant; then she came to know that the applicant is already married.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code, the informant tells that she had seen photographs of the first wife of the applicant on the cell phone and thereafter she came to know about it.
The Court refrains to make deeper scrutiny.
8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 13.08.2024 Avneet/
